newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Postabank Sec gives 'moderate buy' on Zalakeramia.
newsitem.headline: Postabank Sec gives 'moderate buy' on Zalakeramia.

text.p: Hungary's Postabank Securities assigned a "moderate buy" on shares in Hungarian tile maker Zalakeramia Rt, saying the company has a huge growth potential as a result of its recent acquisitions.
In May 1996 it gave a "buy" rating.
Postabank Securities said that Zalakeramia's price was slightly overheated recently, but at the current levels below 7,300 forints they recommended investors to buy the share.
"In the following years the profitability of Zalakeramia group is determined by the performance of the new companies," analysts Ferenc Szollosi and Tamas Hargitai in a company report, dated June 17.

In 1997 Zalakeramia bought majority stakes in Croatian ceramics firm Inker, Hungary's tile maker Pietra and Romanian tile and sanitary products maker Cesarom, but new acquisitions will have only modest impact on Zalakeramia's profits.

"The extra production of the new production line, and the performance of the Romanian company cover the loss of Pietra and Inker, so the new companies will not have significant influence on the 1997 net income of the parent company."
The analysts estimated Zalakeramia's net income, excluding the newly acquired companies, to increase by 16 percent to 941 million forints in 1997.

"This result does not offset the dilution, caused by the capital increase (earlier this year), therefore earnings per share (EPS) decreases from 441 forints in 1996 to 375 forints," Szollosi and Hargitai said.
On the Budapest bourse Zalakeramia closed at 7,250 forints, down 30.
